label: input v at step 3 in sequences starting with u, when v/w came earlier
explanation: A very sparse original-phase feature. It fires only in sequences whose first token is u (100% of activation mass), and only at t=3 (86% of mass) or t=4 (14%). The input there is almost always v (90% of mass). It is strongest when the earlier tokens are also late-alphabet letters v/w, with the top examples being u v w [v] and u w w [v]. Activation is weak when tokens 1-2 are unrelated, e.g. u t s [v] at 0.06. Occasional weak activations also occur on x/3/w inputs after u v w. Even so, most u _ _ v sequences do not activate. The predicate restricted to v/w seen earlier gets about 0.45 precision/recall with 0.68 mass recall on dev. Never fires on the delimiter or in the copy phase, or at t<3 or t>4.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 19 cues. Raise it: orig0=u (+3.34), prev3_tok=u (+2.27), t=4 & in_tok=v (+2.12), t=3 & in_tok=v (+1.56), prev_tok=w (+1.45), recall_idx=-1 & in_tok=v (+1.28). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-2.36), in_first=1 (-1.14), orig8=- (-1.00), in_count=1 (-0.71).
